stories.title: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir speak on phone with Pakistani astronaut aboard China’s Tiangong space station
summary: On Wednesday, Wing Comm­ander Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first foreign astronaut to board China’s Tiangong space station, marking a historic milestone in Pakistan’s space ambitions and Beijing’s efforts to expand its space diplomacy.
China Space Station here I come!” said Wing Commander Ali in Chinese, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

Pakistan’s space agency Suparco and CMSA signed a cooperation agreement in February 2025, under which two Pakistanis were to train in China, with one joining a mission on the Tiangong space station operated by Beijing.

stories.title: PTA says submarine cable fault fixed, internet services return to normal
summary: The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) on Saturday announced the restoration of the SEA-ME-WE 5 (SMW5) international submarine cable system following the repair of a fault, saying internet services across the country had returned to normal.
On November 18, PTA said that a fault had been reported in the SEA-ME-WE 5 (SMW5) international submarine cable system, approximately 11 kilometres from Pakistan’s coast.
In July this year, a fault in the same SMW5 cable system had caused widespread connectivity issues in Pakistan.

stories.title: Building tragedy
summary: FOLLOWING Wednesday’s building collapse in Karachi’s Baloch Colony, the removal or suspension of over a dozen officials has been ordered.
Speaking to journalists, Sindh CM Murad Ali Shah said categorically that such disasters cannot occur without the involvement of government officials.

The Sindh government will have to look within to find answers to why laws are flouted with impunity, why corruption prevails, and why there is reluctance to ensure accountability for those who play with people’s lives.

stories.title: CDA seals Fazl’s Islamabad residence after 'foreign' owner's CNIC cancelled
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Saturday sealed the Islamabad residence of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman after the identity card of the property’s legal owner was cancelled.

CDA highlighted that Amanullah had been given an opportunity of hearing as a show-cause notice was issued to him on Nov 25 to appear personally before the CDA member for Estate on Nov 26 and explain why the change of title in his favour should not be cancelled.
A JUI-F spokesman had confirmed the withdrawal, alleging that Fazl’s Islamabad residence had been cordoned off by capital police and that security personnel had harassed visitors.

stories.title: Lahore ranked world's most polluted major city; Sargodha, Peshawar also record hazardous air
summary: LAHORE: Lahore was ranked the world’s most polluted “major city” on Saturday morning as its air quality index (AQI) reached 400, while Peshawar and Sargodha also recorded AQIs above 400, according to monitoring firm IQAir.

The Swiss air quality monitoring organisation placed Lahore at the top of its ranking for global major cities for the 9am to 10am period on Nov 28, with Kabul second at an AQI of 304 and Delhi third at 238.
The pollution crisis extended beyond Lahore, with several cities across Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa reporting very unhealthy to hazardous air quality.

stories.title: Death toll in Baloch Colony building collapse rises to 11 as rescuers recover three more bodies
summary: KARACHI: Rescue workers recovered three more bodies from the rubble of a six-storey building that collapsed near Karachi’s Baloch Colony area on Saturday, taking the death toll to 11.
In Keamari, 12 of the 19 buildings were sealed and notices were issued to five, while construction work was found to have stopped at one site.
He said that so far, 14 buildings had been sealed in the KAEHS after the building collapse and would be demolished in a second phase of the operation.

stories.title: Driver, student injured as armed men open fire on students’ bus in Charsadda
summary: CHARSADDA: A driver and a student were injured when armed men allegedly opened fire on a coaster carrying students of Institute of Computer and Management Sciences (ICMS) College in the limits of Charsadda’s Nisatta police station late Friday night, police said.
According to Station House Officer (SHO) Nisatta Khan Zaib, two vehicles carrying around 70 students were returning from a recreational trip to Murree when the incident occurred.
According to the coaster driver, who is the complainant in the case, a minor altercation had taken place between students during the trip.

stories.title: Pakistan Railways man booked for transporting dogs in train’s power van in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: During checking at Raiwind Railway Station, the railway police’ special branch staff recovered on Friday two dogs being transported illegally, without booking, in the Allama Iqbal Express (9-Up) power van.
According to officials, the train’s power plant operator, Mohammad Khan, allegedly charged Rs5,000 for transporting the dogs from Karachi, without booking them under the prescribed railway procedure.
The dogs were subsequently booked, and a fine of Rs7,690 was deposited into the railway’s account, officials said.

stories.title: CM Maryam welcomes participants of first paragliding championship in Chakwal
summary: CHAKWAL: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Friday welcomed paragliders at Dharabi Resort for Pakistan’s first-ever paragliding championship.
Chakwal, she noted, was an ancient land, and Pakistan and Punjab were happy to have them.
She told participants that Chakwal had become part of Punjab’s network of 22 cardiac catheterisation laboratories (Cath Labs).

stories.title: City Council approves Rs249m for Karachi's Burns Road Food Street
summary: KARACHI: The City Council on Friday approved a proposal to designate Burns Road Food Street as a pedestrian-only area and allocate an estimated Rs249.823 million for its renovation and development, reviving the initiative that had previously faced judicial intervention.

The resolution was among 34 approved during the general session of the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) City Council, held at the Council Hall under the chairmanship of Deputy Mayor Salman Abdullah Murad.
Responding to criticism, Mayor Wahab said Nehr-i-Khayyam was not the project of any single political party or government but an initiative intended to benefit Karachi’s residents.

stories.title: Sindh Assembly demands uninterrupted gas supply to domestic consumers
summary: The adjournment motion on the issue of prolonged and unannounced gas loadshedding across the province was moved by PPP lawmaker Sumeta Afzal Syed.

Lawmakers across party lines accuse Centre of denying gas-producing province its constitutional right; SSGC urged to inform consumers in advance of any suspension through SMS and media The motion was adopted unanimously after a lengthy debate on the adjournment motion.

Supporting the adjournment motion, PTI MPA Sajid Hussain said that the house had already passed unanimous resolutions on the gas issue and demanded that the federal government be forcefully reminded of Sindh’s rights.

stories.title: Schools directed not to involve students in cleaning, sanitation activities in Punjab
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab School Education Department has prohibited schools from involving students in cleaning and sanitation activities, directing education authorities to ensure strict compliance with the instructions and arrange designated sanitation staff.

The department issued the directive on Nov 27, stating that it had received reports that students in certain public schools were being directed or compelled to undertake cleaning activities, including sweeping classrooms and maintaining cleanliness on school premises.

SED says practice unacceptable and contrary to the fundamental purpose of educational institutions The department directed head teachers and school staff to ensure that no student was subjected to discrimination, coercion or punishment in the name of maintaining cleanliness.

stories.title: Tandoor owners threaten to stop selling roti from Dec 4 in Punjab
summary: LAHORE: Protesting over the increasing actions of the Punjab Enforcement & Regulatory Authority (Pera) Force over using subsidised wheat flour, tandoor owners have announced that they will stop selling rotis from Dec 4 across the city.
The announcement came after the Pera Force started sealing tandoor shops, having wheat flour bags procured on subsidised rates, claiming that tandoors were not authorised to procure subsidised flour.

COMMISSIONER: Lahore Commissioner Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan on Friday visited several sites in the Walled City to review the progress of ongoing development and conservation projects, including work at Mori Gate, Taxali Gate, Sheranwala Gate and Pani Wala Talab.

stories.title: Hope for more survivors revives after man pulled alive from rubble
summary: Families of those trapped in the debris express dissatisfaction with pace of search; DC says operation is continuing uninterrupted For these families, the operation is not merely a rescue effort but an ordeal in which hope and fear remain suspended between life and death.
10 still trapped The Rescue 1122 spokesperson said that 10 people were still missing, as per reports submitted by their relatives at the information desk set up at the site of the collapsed building.
While families of those missing remained dissatisfied with the pace of the search operation, Deputy Commissioner East Kashif Nabi Khuhro said the rescue operation was continuing without interruption.

stories.title: Love at scale
summary: That’s why, she argued before global delegations, when it comes to child protection, “infrastructure is love at scale.” The experience of loving and nurturing support can have a buffering effect for children, tempering the effects of difficult realities.
Chronic economic stress increases the risk of violence within households, as well as of child labour that sends children out without guardrails.
Love at scale cannot mean that children are not seen for their individual circumstances, or are separated from families without working through challenges.

stories.title: JUI-F claims dozens of workers arrested amid protests across KP, Balochistan and Punjab
summary: JUI-F claims dozens of workers arrested amid protests across KP, Balochistan and Punjab

stories.title: Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
summary: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said two of its colleagues, both guards, were killed late Friday in an Israeli strike on one of its clinics in the Gaza Strip.

In the latest attack, two Palestinians were killed in an Israeli strike targeting a gathering of civilians near the Doctors Without Borders office adjacent to Al-Shifa Hospital in western Gaza City, medical sources told Anadolu.
Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza since October 2023 has killed around 75,000 Palestinians, injured more than 176,000, most of them women and children, and destroyed 90% of the enclave’s infrastructure.

stories.title: 'Dar-e-Nijaat' to premiere in Arabic on Saudi channel
summary: Drama Dar-e-Nijaat is set to make its debut in the Arab world on Saudi Arabia-based MBC Bollywood on December 6, with a Syrian Arabic dub, following its popularity in South Asia and fan-organised screenings in India and Bangladesh, Arab News reported.
A source familiar with the broadcast arrangements said MBC acquired the rights and commissioned Syria’s Mesrobian Production to dub the series.

The series will air under the Arabic title “Heena Ghada Al Hob Khalasan” (When Love Became Salvation), from Sunday to Thursday at 6pm Saudi time, according to See Promo, a social media platform that shares MBC Bollywood programming updates.

stories.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for stealing trade secrets
summary: OpenAI sued Apple on Friday, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and discouraging hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices, after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology.

In Friday's filing, OpenAI criticised Apple for encouraging employees to do work on their personal Apple devices and accounts, then preventing those employees from an orderly separation of work and personal accounts when they leave for new jobs.

OpenAI said that Apple continues to access former employees' personal devices and accounts after they leave the company, enabling Apple to "monitor and ensnare departing employees" when they leave for competitors.

stories.title: US forces drove off drones at British air base, Financial Times reports
summary: US forces used counter-drone systems to drive about six drones away from RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk on November 13, the Financial Times reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the incident.
The US Air Force disclosed few details on November 13, saying it had responded to “suspected unauthorised drone activity” and that no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure had been affected.
On Friday, US Air Forces in Europe declined to identify the counter-drone systems it used, citing operational security.

stories.title: Courts yet to settle if men can be prosecuted over ‘marital rape’: report
summary: It noted that the Protection of Women (Criminal Law Amendment) Act, 2006 redefined rape under Section 375 of the Pakistan Penal Code without reference to marital status, so marital rape can in principle attract the same penalty as any other rape.

The World Health Organisation estimates cited in the report put lifetime intimate partner violence in Pakistan at 24.8pc, below Afghanistan (50.9pc), Bangladesh (48.9pc) and India (29.9pc), though the figures do not isolate marital rape.
Pakistan ranks sixth globally among countries with the highest number of child marriages, while more than 19 million women and girls in the country were married before the age of 18.

stories.title: US military says cyber systems secure after reports of Air Force hack
summary: The United States military denied Friday any issues with its computer security following media reports that the Air Force's cloud based system was hacked, in what would be the latest high profile breach of US digital infrastructure in recent weeks.
The reported attack is the latest in a string of major outages in US government and private-sector digital infrastructure.
AFP was hit by a cyberattack on Thursday, forcing a major client-facing system to be taken offline.

stories.title: PM calls for stronger Pak-Oman ties
summary: Chairing a meeting on matters related to the PCSIR, the prime minister said the institution could play a significant role in helping Pakistani products compete in international markets.

The prime minister also called for stronger cooperation between the PCSIR and the National Vocational and Technical Train­ing Commission (NAVTTC) to improve industrial and technical training opportunities for young people.
The prime minister constituted a committee to review the PCSIR’s mandate, performance and future role.

stories.title: AJK PM extends olive branch to protesters in Rawalakot
summary: Mr Gillani said the government would also introduce housing loans for deserving people, improve sanitation in all 10 district headquarters and undertake beautification projects in Muzaffarabad.
Call for dialogue Earlier, Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq said the government had assumed office to serve the people and promote development and public welfare.
Referring to a recently adopted Assembly resolution, he said it reflected the common position of the people of AJK, the PML-N and all political parties represented in the legislature.

stories.title: 14 found dead on migrant boat off Spain's Canary Islands
summary: 14 migrants were found dead after a boat carrying about 100 people was rescued near Spain's Canary Islands, Spanish news agency EFE reported on Friday, as a surge in arrivals overwhelms authorities in the region.

Read: Spain deports asylum seekers 84 survivors disembarked from a separate boat at the island's La Restinga port, home to a migrant reception centre and field hospital where most migrant boats reaching the island have been processed.

Daily arrivals hit all-time high Migrant arrivals to the Canary Islands have accelerated since October, hitting a record 2,100 people in a single day on November 25, most of them coming to El Hierro, population 11,400.

stories.title: Gaza weather system threatens 1.3m Palestinians with humanitarian disaster
summary: More than 1.3 million Palestinians living in deteriorating tents face a potential humanitarian disaster as a severe weather system is expected to hit the enclave within days, Gaza’s Civil Defence warned Friday.

Basal said the continuation of current conditions constitutes a clear violation of Palestinians’ rights, dignity and privacy, warning that the approaching weather system would not be the last to strike Gaza during the winter.

On November 6, a severe weather system hit Gaza, killing five Palestinians, including two women and three children, after a sand embankment collapsed onto tents housing displaced people in the central city of Deir al-Balah, according to the Civil Defence.

stories.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi cruise missile fired toward capital Riyadh
summary: The Saudi-led coalition said on Saturday that air defences intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the Houthi group toward the Saudi capital, Riyadh.
Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting Yemen's government against the Houthis since 2015.
The group has controlled the capital, Sanaa, and parts of Yemen since 2014.

stories.title: Karachi building collapse: Death toll rises to 11 as rescue teams recover three more bodies
summary: The suspects included relatives of the contractor, while the building's owner and contractor were not produced before the court.
Also read: CM Murad orders removal of SBCA chief, suspension of 16 officers over Karachi building collapse The counsel also questioned whether any officials of the SBCA had been arrested.
One of the suspects maintained that they had been produced before the court as though they were the building's owners.

stories.title: CDA to set up special fund to tackle smog in Islamabad
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Friday decided to create a special fund for smog mitigation, environmental improvement and research and development projects.
The said decision and several other decisions regarding smog mitigation and environmental improvement were taken in a meeting held here with CDA Chairman Sohail Ashraf in the chair.
It said that the meeting decided that a special fund will also be created for smog mitigation, environmental improvement and research and development projects.

stories.title: Punjab approves Rs5.886bn project to restore Rawalpindi’s Walled City
summary: Following the cabinet’s approval, sites such as the Bagh Sardaran Complex, Jamia Masjid, Haveli Sujan Singh, Haveli Mohan Singh, Krishna Temple, Haveli Durga Niwas, Kalyan Das Mandir and Khurshid Cinema have been designated as protected heritage sites.
In 1903, local Muslims of Rawalpindi constructed the building through donations to serve as a central place of worship during British rule.
Haveli Durga Niwas is a historic pre-Partition haveli in Old Rawalpindi, built in 1934 by wealthy Sikh coal merchant Sardar Budh Singh Sawhney for his wife, Durga Devi.

stories.title: Three-day Sikh celebrations end with Bhog ceremony
summary: The concluding day’s proceedings centred on the sacred Bhog ritual, symbolising the completion of the religious observances, while special prayers brought the congregation together in an atmosphere of devotion, reverence and spiritual fulfilment.

Having completed their religious obligations and offered prayers at the historic shrine, the visiting pilgrims subsequently left Hassanabdal for Kartarpur, the next destination on their pilgrimage to Pakistan’s sacred Sikh sites.

For the visiting devotees, the pilgrimage offered an opportunity not only to fulfil their religious obligations but also to experience the historical and spiritual heritage associated with one of the most important Sikh shrines in the region.

stories.title: Seven terrorists killed in Bannu operation
summary: BANNU/SWABI: Security forces killed seven terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in the Shoikhel area of Bakakhel tehsil in Bannu district, official sources said on Friday.
The sources claimed that seven suspected militants were killed in the operation.
Earlier, on Nov 6, a suspected militant was killed during an operation in the mountainous area of Rocha in Bakakhel.

stories.title: Two ‘street criminals’ arrested in Peshawar action
summary: PESHAWAR: The city police on Friday arrested two suspected street criminals in an injured condition during separate encounters and recovered stolen valuables from their possession.
Shahpur and Fakirabad police stations engaged street criminals in separate encounters, arresting two dangerous snatchers in an injured condition, according to a statement issued here.
The injured suspects were wanted by police in several criminal cases and incidents of street crime.

stories.title: PHC upholds Tirah operation, declares it in domain of executive policy making
summary: PESHAWAR: Upholding the launch of a military operation in Tirah Valley early this year, the Peshawar High Court has ruled that undertaking counter-terrorism operations falls within the sphere of executive policy and operational discretion.
The bench also observed that the collateral damage didn’t, by itself, render a security operation unlawful.

The bench observed that it expected the federal and provincial governments would give due consideration to the formulation of such a framework in consultation with the relevant authorities and stakeholders.

stories.title: Ahsan seeks zero-tariff access to Chinese market
summary: Plan to boost Pakistan’s exports to $25bn Mr Iqbal also sought support for the proposed Pakistan-China Knowledge Corridor, envisaging doctoral studies and specialised research opportunities for around 10,000 Pakistani scholars over 10 years.

Discussing the second phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), he identified industrial and agricultural cooperation, business partnerships, technology transfer, minerals and green development as key priorities.
He linked the next phase of CPEC with Pakistan’s URAAN development programme and China’s 15th Five-Year Plan, emphasising the importance of policy continuity.

stories.title: AJK Overseas Commission reconstituted
summary: The commission’s ex-officio members include the chief secretary, Senior Member Board of Revenue (SMBR), and secretaries of law, justice, parliamentary affairs and human rights; finance; planning and development; and industries, mineral resources and labour.
The additional secretary of the Home Department will also serve as a member.
The post of commissioner, who will serve as the commission’s member-secretary, will be notified separately on the commission’s recommendations.

stories.title: CM Bugti calls on Baloch youth to shun extremism
summary: Addressing students, Mr Bugti emphasised encouraging meaningful discussions on the political struggle of the Baloch people, different political ideologies and future paths.

Mr Bugti said the Balochistan government was ready to listen to critical opinions and development-related grievances through direct engagement, noting the province offered higher education at lower fees than other provinces.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr Bugti said it had been made clear on the assembly floor from the first day that no government jobs in Balochistan would be sold off.

stories.title: Farmer buying fertiliser to earn livelihood is a consumer: LHC
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court has held that a self-employed farmer who purchases fertilisers solely to earn his livelihood is a “consumer” under the Punjab Consumer Protection Act, 2005, setting aside a consumer court order dismissing a grower’s complaint.

On April 23, 2024, the consumer court dismissed his complaint at the outset, holding that the fertiliser had been purchased for a commercial purpose and that the appellant did not qualify as a consumer.
He further observed that the consumer court had inferred commercial purpose merely from the appellant’s reference to profit, without examining whether farming was his means of livelihood.

stories.title: Call for ‘affordable’ diagnostic facilities, medicines to treat genetic disorders
summary: He urged medical professionals receiving fellowships to demonstrate greater commitment towards patients with rare diseases, saying professional recognition brought greater responsibilities towards affected children and their families.
He said cousin marriages accounted for 60 to 70 per cent of marriages in Pakistan, while approximately 70pc of rare diseases had a genetic origin.
He also called for establishing a national registry of rare diseases, saying Pakistan lacked reliable data on the prevalence and burden of these disorders.

stories.title: US Central Command denies Iranian commander's claims about seized tankers, carrier strike, Hormuz toll
summary: The US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM) denied multiple claims Friday by an Iranian military commander about American forces, saying Washington did not steal two Iranian oil tankers and that no toll is charged to ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

The entire situation the Iranian military commander described is another fabricated lie," CENTCOM wrote on US social media platform X, rejecting a claim that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy retook two tankers while American troops on board slept.

An Iranian military commander made multiple FALSE claims concerning U.S. Forces over the past 24 hours: 🚫 CLAIM: The U.S. military stole two Iranian oil tankers and the IRGC’s navy retook the vessels while American troops on board slept. ✅ FACT: Iran no longer has a navy.
